purpose: Defensive publication. This ledger exists so that a dated, citable record of each contribution is public, which defeats a later claim of invention WITHOUT anyone having to prove a universal negative. It does not assert novelty: 'no prior art exists' quantifies over everything ever published and no finite search decides it, so novelty is bound to the axiom no_prior_art_is_undecidable and never to a seal.
notALegalInstrument: This is a record, not advice and not a filing. Patent priority, jurisdiction and filing strategy are a solicitor's work. What a defensive publication does is make the art public and dated; what it does not do is grant anything.

ratchet.what: Twelve measured surfaces whose ceilings only move down, failing on unrecorded improvement as well as on growth, with each deliberate raise recorded with its reason.

citations.text: Ratcheting quality gates on new code are established practice; the mechanism is widely deployed rather than published under one citation.

measure-fingerprinting.what: Each measure's implementation is fingerprinted from its syntax tree printed WITHOUT comments, so rewording a measure is free and changing what it counts fails until declared.

criterion-modules.what: Predicates that decide whether a subject meets a named standard, each condition drawn from a theory with an operational commitment, each written to reject its own cheap pass, and each stating what would refute it. Six gate a release.

citationPolicy: Every claim of known art carries a RESOLVABLE identifier where one exists, and says so when one does not. `resolved` records whether the identifier was actually fetched and confirmed to name the cited work — not whether the author believes it. An unresolved DOI is a DOI nobody has checked, and this ledger prints how many there are rather than letting a plausible-looking string pass for a citation. Identifiers written from memory are exactly the kind of claim this repository exists to refuse, so they start unresolved. All nine DOIs were resolved against Crossref on 2026-09-04 and each returned the title of the work cited; the returned title is recorded beside the identifier so a reader can see WHAT resolved, not merely that something did.
